name: Ovex DutyBand Court-Issue Ankle Monitor
description: Matte black polymer housing, 38mm thick, locked to the ankle by a tamper-evident ratchet band in high-visibility yellow. The status light pulses green every four seconds when compliant; amber when near a restricted zone; red when a violation is logged. Ovex manufacturing marks are embossed on the outer face. Impossible to disguise under most pants legs. Designed to be seen — the visibility is the point.
functionality: Continuous GPS tracking with 10-meter precision. BCI-ping broadcasts wearer ID to law enforcement nodes within 50 meters. Tamper detection triggers immediate alert. Battery charged remotely by municipal grid — wearer cannot deactivate. Logs all zone breaches with timestamp.
what_it_says: The system knows exactly where this person is at all times, and everyone around them knows it too.
worn_by: Tier 1 residents on conditional housing agreements
price_range: Φ0 (court-issued) / Φ180–Φ400 (compliance fee billed to wearer monthly)
story_hooks: A fixer claims she can spoof the GPS ping for Φ600 — but three of her last clients disappeared within a week of the job.
The monitor on a Tier 1 resident starts pulsing red inside his own apartment, flagging a zone he's never left — and no one at Ovex will explain why.
A street tech discovers the monitors broadcast on a secondary frequency that no court order authorized — someone is listening to more than location data.
